finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side. The only check is a startswith('https://') string test. There is no host or IP validation, so internal HTTPS services, link-local and metadata endpoints, and loopback or private hosts are reachable. axios follows redirects by default (up to 5), so an attacker's https server can 302 to http://169.254.169.254/ or http://users.internal:8080/. DNS names that resolve to private IPs also pass. The response only returns the byte length, so this is semi-blind. It still leaks size and reachability, and the request itself can trigger side effects on internal services. No auth guard is present on the route.

trace.note: Route handler with no auth middleware
Only check: typeof string and startsWith('https://')
Response size is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Scheme prefix check on the raw string only. No parsed-host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, no DNS pinning, no redirect restriction (maxRedirects not set), no auth. The /users/:id route (line 20) was checked and is not SSRF: the host is a constant and the id is encodeURIComponent'd.

verdict.guard_found: none (only typeof string + startsWith('https://') prefix check at server.js:11; no auth middleware, no host/IP validation, no maxRedirects limit)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated route (server.js:9), only a prefix check at server.js:11 guards it, and it reaches axios.get(url) at server.js:14 with default redirects, returning the byte length at server.js:15.
